name: Minimally invasive tissue sampling (MITS)
definition: A postmortem approach that collects small tissue and fluid samples to help investigate cause of death. The linked CHAMPS publication describes standardized specimen collection and histology procedures.
source_name: CHAMPS MITS standardization study, CDC Stacks

name: Hematoxylin and eosin staining (H&E)
definition: A routine stain using two dyes. Hematoxylin colors nuclei blue to purple; eosin colors cytoplasm and supporting tissue pink to red, making tissue structure easier to examine.

name: Squames
definition: Superficial, keratinized squamous cells, often lacking a nucleus. The linked IARC atlas describes this term in cervical cytology; its significance in a MITS specimen depends on the tissue and report context.
source_name: IARC Histopathology and Cytopathology Atlas glossary
